The documented cmds child environment is exact: Guarded.env copies only PATH/HOME/LANG/TMPDIR when present, appends MRV_RUN_ID, then the workflow-declared env names. That precision is what makes the separate 'the binary reads exactly these env names' bullet read as an equally exhaustive statement (see the medium finding).

findings.note: SKILL.md:81-83 states, in the section headed 'Trust boundary (read before passing any knob)', that 'The binary reads exactly these env names: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, OPENAI_BASE_URL, METAREVIEW_JUDGE_MODEL, METAREVIEW_JUDGE_EFFORT, MOCK_AI, MRV_RUN_ID, HOME (plus PATH and, on Linux, SSL_CERT_* through the Go runtime). No proxy variables are honoured.' The list is presented as closed and explicitly accounts for names read by the Go runtime rather than by metareview code, so it invites an operator to treat anything absent from it as irrelevant. Two things are missing. (1) TMPDIR: internal/fsm/gate/git.go:249 calls os.MkdirTemp("", "mrv-index-*"), which on unix resolves through os.TempDir() to $TMPDIR, and that directory is where the scratch git index for the working-tree hash is created (WorkTree is on the normal advance path). I reproduced it: a program calling os.MkdirTemp("", "mrv-index-*") with TMPDIR pointed at a scratch directory created mrv-index-* inside it. So TMPDIR is read by the binary and steers where it writes, and the same document already names TMPDIR one bullet earlier as part of the cmds child environment - the omission is inconsistent inside a single section. (2) The codex arm: internal/fsm/cli/deps.go:101-103 builds exec.CommandContext without setting cmd.Env, so the spawned `codex` process inherits the entire parent environment - every proxy variable, every API key, everything. The doc's neighbouring bullet (SKILL.md:76-79) goes out of its way to reassure that 'metareview never handles that credential and no API key is required for it' and that the spawn sits outside the allowed_cmds consent gate, but never says the child gets the whole environment, in pointed contrast to the exactly-enumerated cmds child env. Net effect: for a codex/ judge the closed env set and 'no proxy variables are honoured' do not describe the process metareview actually runs. Both are one-line doc fixes: add TMPDIR (os.MkdirTemp) to the enumeration, and state that the codex child inherits the full environment (unlike a consented cmd). Note the same closed list in docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-cli.md:356-359 omits TMPDIR too, so fixing the skill without the spec would leave the stale copy behind - the identical-guard-at-another-layer pattern.

evidence.note: 'The binary reads exactly these env names: ...' - the word 'exactly', plus the parenthetical covering PATH and SSL_CERT_* 'through the Go runtime', makes this an exhaustive claim about runtime-read names as well.

dir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "mrv-index-*") - empty dir argument means os.TempDir(), i.e. $TMPDIR on unix. Verified experimentally: TMPDIR=<scratch> made the mrv-index-* directory appear under <scratch>.

func realCodexExec: cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, codexBin, args...) with cmd.Env left nil, so os.Environ() is inherited wholesale by the codex child; the function's own comment says 'the environment is inherited' but SKILL.md never surfaces that.

findings.note: ERR_REPO_ROOT_MISMATCH is undocumented anywhere a driver will look, and the skill's exit-2 rule is unactionable for it. SKILL.md:32 says exit 2 means 'usage, or a refusal before anything was recorded: fix the input and retry - unless the code is a consent (ERR_CMDS_NOT_ALLOWED) or escalation (ERR_RUN_ESCALATED) code'. envelope.go:55 puts ERR_REPO_ROOT_MISMATCH in the exit-2 set, but it is raised when the checkout moved (mock runs are path-bound), which no amount of 'fix the input and retry' resolves; an agent following the skill literally will retry forever or give up without telling the human what actually happened. docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-cli.md:361-362 lists 'a moved checkout -> ERR_REPO_ROOT_MISMATCH (mock runs are path-bound)' as required content for skills/fsm/SKILL.md + commands/fsm.md, and grep over all non-spec Markdown finds the code in none of them (nor in docs/fsm/driving-a-workflow.md). One clause in the exit-2 row fixes it.

evidence.note: exit-2 row names only ERR_CMDS_NOT_ALLOWED and ERR_RUN_ESCALATED as the codes that are not retry-after-fixing-the-input.
exit2 map includes CodeRepoRootMismatch = "ERR_REPO_ROOT_MISMATCH" (envelope.go:22), so it surfaces as exit 2 with the doc's misleading advice attached.

findings.note: Two lines in SKILL.md are unusable as written by the audience the skill targets. (a) SKILL.md:75 ends the model bullet with 'high effort is Go-only'. A driving agent cannot decode that: it is not a constraint on the CLI at all - judge.go:101 accepts high on every provider - it is spec shorthand (docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-judge-kinds.md:329) meaning the Go judge ADDS the high level relative to the reference implementation's table. As phrased it reads like a restriction and will be acted on as one. Either drop it from the skill or say 'high is metareview's own addition to the provider tables'. (b) SKILL.md:23 says 'If you do not know where a run is: metareview fsm state --run <id>' - the case where you do not know where the run is is precisely the case where --run may be unavailable, and both the authoritative contract (internal/fsm/cli/prompt.go:7) and commands/fsm.md render this as bare `metareview fsm state`, which resolves flag -> MRV_RUN_ID -> newest non-errored run (wiring.go:219). The skill's variant is the only copy of the three that requires the id.

evidence.note: '... plus codex/<model> ids judged through the Codex CLI; `high` effort is Go-only.' - contrast judge.go:101 var efforts = {low, medium, high, xhigh}, which accepts high for both HTTP providers.
